title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says US & China must work together for AI safety
key_facts: Huang said the US 'absolutely must' work with Chinese AI companies so the technology advances safely, per CNBC
He called AI 'powerful and potentially dangerous' and said 'dialogue' is the mechanism
He said he keeps dialogues with many researchers in China and advised the UK to do likewise
Remarks followed Nvidia's $250 million, five-year donation to UK AI safety and security research
He said AI should be treated as critical infrastructure like electricity or water and opposed overly restrictive rules
In a Bloomberg interview he called delayed AI IPOs and blocked data centre projects 'growing pains'
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent raised a US-China AI dialogue with China's He Lifeng in September
quote_evidence: Nvidia (NVDA) Chief Executive Jensen Huang said Wednesday that the United States "absolutely must" work with Chinese AI companies to manage risks around a technology he described as "powerful and potentially dangerous."
"We ought to enhance the dialogue," he said. "The United States should do it... I advocated that the U.K. do the same thing."
why_it_matters_hint: A leading AI supplier is pushing both governments toward AI safety talks.
notes: CNBC and the CNA clip were blocked or empty; text read via BigGo Finance, which summarises the CNBC report. Huang spoke Wed 14 Oct in London; reporting is 15 Oct. Url is the CNBC link named by the search result.
